title: saṅkhatā
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.

paras.en: “And how, bhikkhus, should one know, how should one see, for the immediate destruction of the āsavas to occur?

Here, bhikkhus, the uninstructed ordinary person,
who is not a seer of the noble ones and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma, who is not a seer of superior persons and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma, regards material form as self.

That regarding, bhikkhus, is a saṅkhāra. This saṅkhāra — what is its source, what is its origin,
from what is it born and produced?

When the uninstructed ordinary person experiences
what is felt, born of contact accompanied by ignorance,
craving arises: because of that, this saṅkhāra is born.

Thus, bhikkhus, that saṅkhāra is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen; that craving is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen; that vedanā is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen; that contact is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen; that ignorance is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen. When one knows and sees thus, bhikkhus, the immediate destruction of the āsavas occurs.”
